answer: Tie each agent to a physically metered site. A node streams signed micro-readings: the local zephyr's gust profile, barometric drift across its mesa plateau, and the gamma signature of the shale bedrock under it. Verifiers randomly demand the next 30-second reading and cross-check it against two independent neighbors; a mismatch burns a 50-token bond. Each identity needs its own $400 sensor fixed at a distinct coordinate, so a farm can't clone or parallelize one rig into 1,000 fakes — every sybil repays the full hardware and siting cost.
